# Results — Study 868 (Global Curve-Slope Carry)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
fixed-income *roll + carry* / curve-carry literature (Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen & Vrugt
2018, *"Carry"*; the roll-down argument): a **steep** yield curve pays a duration holder,
so ranking bond markets by a curve-steepness / carry proxy and going **long the high-carry
/ steep-curve, short the flat / low-carry** markets should earn a positive costed net
Sharpe. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current
month is dropped; **as-of 2026-06-30**). Fingerprint `63122f29382a` (month-end price panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), resampled to **month-end**, **6 sovereign-bond ETFs**, 2007-01-31 → 2026-06-30, **234** months (215 after the 36-month carry burn-in) |
| Universe | `SHY` (1-3y UST), `IEF` (7-10y UST), `TLT` (20y+ UST), `BWX` (ex-US developed, unhedged), `IGOV` (ex-US developed, unhedged), `BNDX` (USD-hedged global ex-US) — cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Carry proxy | each sleeve's **trailing 36-month realized yield** (annualised mean monthly total return) ÷ its **published effective duration** = a *yield-to-duration* / carry-per-unit-rate-risk score (durations: SHY 1.85, IEF 7.3, TLT 16.4, BWX 7.9, IGOV 8.1, BNDX 6.9 yrs); known at the close of month `t−1` |
| Book | **cross-sectional**: split the markets at the cross-sectional median of the carry proxy; **long** the above-median (high-carry) sleeves, **short** the below-median (low-carry), equal-weight within each leg, dollar-neutral; book return = `mean(long r_t) − mean(short r_t)` |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: proxy through close `t−1` → hold month `t`. The costed backtest charges one-way `cost_bps × turnover` per rebalance and `75 bps/yr` borrow on the short-weighted NAV |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the monthly book; one-sample *t*; a 3,000-draw column-permutation placebo; a three-era robustness cut; a 24/36/48/60-month window sweep; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship & power — named on the Signal axis.** These six are *currently listed,
surviving* funds; wound-up global-sovereign ETFs are absent, so any positive carry result
is a **mild upper bound**. The USD-hedged `BNDX` lists only from 2013, so the full
six-market cross-section is short and the panel is tiny by construction — both facts
**limit statistical power**. And with only *total-return* prices the carry/yield is a
**proxy** (a long-window realized-yield, not a clean forward yield); a long window is used
precisely so transient price trends average out. All three caveats travel with the numbers.

## Benchmark — naive equal-weight buy-and-hold

Owning all six ETFs equal-weight, no ranking at all:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean | **+21.36 bps/mo** (+2.56 %/yr) |
| Sharpe | 0.398 |
| Newey-West(6) *t* | +1.79 |

This is the honest yardstick: any "carry edge" has to beat *just holding the bonds*.

## The headline — yield-to-duration carry (`long high-carry / short low-carry`)

n = **215** months:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **mean book return** | **−20.17 bps/mo** (−2.42 %/yr) |
| long leg / short leg | +9.99 bps / **+30.16 bps** |
| annualised vol | 8.10 % |
| Sharpe | **−0.299** |
| **Newey-West(6) *t*** | **−1.45** |
| one-sample *t* | −1.27 |
| hit rate | 0.447 |

The yield-to-duration sort earns the **wrong sign**: the "low-carry" short leg (+30.16
bps/mo) *out-earns* the "high-carry" long leg (+9.99 bps/mo), so the long-minus-low book is
**negative** (−20.17 bps/mo). It does not clear the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar in magnitude (NW *t* =
−1.45), but there is certainly no positive carry premium here — if anything the sort is
perversely inverted (dividing by duration tilts long into the low-yielding short end, which
lagged).

## The headline — raw realized-yield carry (`long high-yield / short low-yield`)

The plainer proxy (rank by realized yield, no duration scaling), same 215 months:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **mean book return** | **+3.16 bps/mo** (+0.38 %/yr) |
| long leg / short leg | +16.98 bps / +13.82 bps |
| Sharpe | 0.043 |
| **Newey-West(6) *t*** | **+0.20** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.18 |

The raw carry sort has the right sign but is **dead flat** — +3.16 bps/mo, NW *t* = +0.20.
No cross-sectional carry premium survives.

## Placebo — is there any carry information at all?

Keep the carry-rank long/short weights but **permute which market's forward return feeds
each rank** (breaks the carry → forward-return link, preserves each month's cross-sectional
return spread), 3,000 draws:

| variant | observed | null mean (sd) | right-tail *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| yield-to-duration | −20.17 bps | −0.23 bps (10.91) | 0.939 |
| raw realized-yield | +3.16 bps | −0.03 bps (7.70) | 0.439 |

The yield-to-duration observation sits deep in the **wrong** (left) tail — a random
assignment of markets to legs beats the carry sort 94 % of the time. The raw-carry
observation sits **squarely inside** its null (*p* = 0.44). Neither proxy carries
cross-sectional carry information beyond noise.

## Robustness — three eras

| era | yield-to-duration | | raw realized-yield | |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| | mean | NW *t* | mean | NW *t* |
| 2010-2016 (n=72) | −11.37 bps | −0.38 | +41.59 bps | +1.23 |
| 2016-2021 (n=60) | **−40.24 bps** | **−3.02** | −30.08 bps | −1.70 |
| 2021-2026 (n=66) | +2.27 bps | +0.13 | +7.17 bps | +0.42 |

No era shows a robust *positive* carry premium; the only |*t*| ≥ 2 reading is the
**wrong-sign** 2016-2021 yield-to-duration book (−40.24 bps, *t* = −3.02). The two proxies
even disagree on sign era-by-era — the result is not a stable premium, it is noise. And the
**window sweep** (yield-to-duration NW *t*: 24m −1.70, 36m −1.45, 48m −0.46, 60m +0.29)
flips sign as the formation window lengthens — fragile in the proxy parameter.

## The costed backtest — can you get paid for it?

One-way `cost_bps × turnover` per rebalance; short book pays 75 bps/yr borrow.

| variant | one-way | gross/mo | cost/mo | net/mo | net Sharpe | *t* (net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| yield-to-duration | 5 bps | −20.17 | 8.07 | **−28.24 bps** | −0.419 | −1.77 |
| yield-to-duration | 10 bps | −20.17 | 9.89 | **−30.06 bps** | −0.446 | −1.89 |
| raw realized-yield | 5 bps | +3.16 | 7.97 | **−4.81 bps** | −0.066 | −0.28 |
| raw realized-yield | 10 bps | +3.16 | 9.69 | **−6.53 bps** | −0.089 | −0.38 |

Both books turn over ~0.34-0.36 of NAV per month (~8-10 bps/mo of friction) and both go
**negative** net of costs — the yield-to-duration book was already losing money gross, and
the raw-carry book's thin +3.16 bps gross is eaten whole by the first cost. No costed net
edge exists.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded monthly panel where each market carries a **fixed structural carry
level**; with `edge > 0` the high-carry markets persistently out-yield and the
trailing-yield sort recovers them. No network.

| world | mean NW *t* | fires (\|t\| ≥ 2) |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | **−0.05** | **2/20** |
| planted (`edge = 0.010`), **20 seeds** | **+18.17** (mean Sharpe 3.50) | **20/20** |

The detector recovers a *planted* cross-sectional carry effect cleanly and essentially
never fires on the equal-yield null — so the flat/wrong-sign real-tape result is a genuine
absence of edge, not a broken engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited
in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed global curve-slope carry premium does **not** appear on
  this tape. The primary **yield-to-duration** sort earns the **wrong sign** (−20.17
  bps/mo, NW *t* = −1.45; column-permutation placebo *p* = 0.94 — a random leg assignment
  beats it 94 % of the time; its low-carry short leg out-earns its high-carry long leg),
  and its only significant era is wrong-signed (2016-2021: −40.24 bps, *t* = −3.02). The
  plainer **raw realized-yield** sort is **dead flat** (+3.16 bps/mo, NW *t* = +0.20,
  placebo *p* = 0.44). Both flip sign across eras and formation windows. A clean 20-seed
  synthetic control fires on a planted carry (mean *t* = +18.17, 2/20 on the null) — so the
  null is real, not a broken engine.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Every variant loses money once costed (yield-to-duration net
  −28.24 bps/mo at 5 bps, raw carry net −4.81 bps/mo at 5 bps; net Sharpe < 0 in all cases)
  on ~0.35 monthly turnover plus short borrow. No costed net edge survives.
